blocks.text: IP address objects are reusable components that allow you to organize your network resources. These objects can contain IP addresses, Classless Inter-Domain Routings (CIDRs), and FQDNs. They allow you to use a single-named object as the source or destination criteria when configuring VPN access policies.
IP address objects provide the following benefits and enable you to:

blocks.item: Centralize the management of your network resources. If an IP address changes, you only need to update the object, and all policies that reference it are automatically updated.
Simplify auditing and make policy rules self-documenting. A rule using a named object is easier to understand than one with manually entered IP addresses.

blocks.heading: About the IP Address Object Page

blocks.text: On the IP Address Object page (Private Access > VPN (for Legacy Apps) > VPN Access Policy IP Address), you can do the following:

blocks.item: Search for an IP address object by its name.
View a list of all configured IP address objects. For each object, you can see:
Name: The name of the IP address object.
Networks: The networks grouped in the IP address object.
Modify the columns displayed in the table.
Display more rows or a different page of the table.
Go to the Access Policies page to view VPN access policy rules.
Go to the IdP Attribute Object page to view IdP attribute objects.
